title: HOOP: A Scalable Hybrid DC-DC Converter Ring for High-Performance Computing
problem: Multi-phase DC-DC converters for AI-era HPC require automatic current balancing across tens or hundreds of phases without complex digital control; hybrid topologies in parallel remain difficult to balance between converters.
motivation: AI computing demands exponentially higher power delivery with stronger capability, higher efficiency, and faster response. As N phases increase, manual current-balance control complexity scales, creating bottleneck for scalable power delivery.
method: HOOP arranges multiple hybrid DC-DC converters (each using multiple power stages) in a ring topology—connecting them in a closed loop. Within this ring, a power path circulates electricity to naturally spread the current load evenly across all converters, while a separate control path allows individual stages to be switched off when unneeded. This works because capacitors (energy-storage components) inherently share electrical charge when connected together, a principle that simple single-stage converters rely on, but here it extends across multiple parallel converters connected via the ring.
key_novelty: Connecting hybrid converters in a ring topology allows them to automatically balance current without a separate digital controller.
contributions: Inherent auto-current-balancing characteristic across N phases without global digital control
Hybrid converter topology scalable to hundreds of parallel phases
Phase shedding via back ring for efficiency at variable loads
Simplifies power delivery system design for AI accelerators and HPC
baselines: Conventional multi-phase converters with digital control
Prior buck/three-level charge-balance approaches (single converter only)
limitations: Abstract does not provide specific efficiency numbers, voltage droop performance, or silicon area metrics.
primary_theme: Scalable auto-balancing power delivery via converter rings
